svg.title: The riverside promenade the player walks: a LIMESTONE SLAB pavement - six courses graded so the near ones are taller, a 96 px slab period staggered half a slab per course, adjacent slabs in different tones - behind a low limestone parapet with piers over the river, with lamps, benches, planters, three street trees in early-autumn gold and green, and six people. Two sett courses then four slab courses, the near ones much taller: SLABS AND NOT PLANKS, deliberately: Halifax's tile is a timber deck and read as pavement once already, so this level's pavement is drawn as what it is, with a cross-joint grid rather than long boards, and its parapet is stone rather than a timber kerb. Every object is a TYPE - a plain lamp standard, a plain bench, a plain planter - because this tile repeats every 1920 px and furniture that is really architecture is architecture. The six figures stand at the parapet, across the promenade, which is why they are drawn at about 165 px rather than the player's 420; they are six heads tall like every character in the game and carry no cultural marker of any kind. World y 800..1320; local y 480 IS the ground line at world 1280, and the tile is opaque from world 1150 down. The tile is 80 px taller than the band it needs, and the whole drawing is translated down by that much, so the tallest street tree's canopy is not clipped by the tile's own top edge - which it was at 440.
